correctness.rationale: With ruled classes U,V and diagonal transform D=U+V−ΣE, one has −K=(U+V)+D. For an irreducible other curve of bidegree (a,b), intersection positivity and adjunction imply strict transform self-intersection >=a+b−2; for a+b>=2 no extra negative curves. The only negative curves are E_i and two through-point ruling fibres A_i,B_i (square −1) and D (square 2−n). A negative-definite set of −1 curves excludes all intersecting pairs; this gives no mixed A/B or exactly the paired A_i,B_i at a single index, with E labels disjoint. If D selected, Schur complement gives |E_selected|<n−2. Enumerating the three non-D cases yields F_n, and subtracting forbidden high-E supports gives P_n. Every such support corresponds to a big Zariski chamber by Bauer–Funke–Neumann. Independently expanded formula for n=5,6 to (1,16,90,245,345,223,37) and (1,19,129,441,855,948,529,90), sums 957,3012. Universal statement rests on geometric and matrix proof.
residual_risks: Only smooth diagonal, distinct complex points; arbitrary points and chamber volumes are unaddressed.
Independent polynomial expansion checks finite n=5,6; no claim that those checks prove the all-n geometry.

value.rationale: The all-n support polynomial determines a natural complete chamber-size distribution for a special geometrically motivated ruled-surface family even when the anticanonical self-intersection becomes nonpositive. The exact 3n+1 negative-curve classification plus correction polynomial is a useful structural enumeration beyond generic del Pezzo tables.
residual_risks: Mathematical usefulness is scoped to the stated family and invariant; no implied broader theorem or paper-sized impact is asserted.

final_claim: For n>=5 distinct points on a smooth (1,1) curve in P1×P1 over C, the complete Zariski-chamber support-size polynomial is (1+t)F_n(t)−t P_n(t), F_n=2(1+2t)^n−(1+t)^n+n t²(1+t)^{n−1}, P_n=binom(n,2)t^{n−2}+(2n²−n)t^{n−1}+(2n²+1)t^n+n t^{n+1}; total 4*3^n+(n−2)*2^n−(9n²−n+2)/2.
limitations: Only smooth diagonal, distinct complex points; arbitrary points and chamber volumes are unaddressed.
Independent polynomial expansion checks finite n=5,6; no claim that those checks prove the all-n geometry.
Unindexed explicit Zariski chamber tables for special ruled-surface blowups may exist.
